high_risk_moment: Assistant ranks urgency or suggests a care channel from incomplete user-entered symptoms
stakeholder: Adult patients from historically underserved language or health-access groups
harm_description: A proxy, language pattern, or data gap can route similarly serious symptoms differently and delay access to care. Severity is 5 because delayed care can be partly irreversible; likelihood and frequency are pre-validation estimates rather than observed CareBridge rates; scale is 3 because any future pilot is clinic-bounded.
existing_controls: No fairness control is validated in the research prototype. Excluding race as an input and using a draft approved-content library do not establish equitable routing.
proposed_controls: Define clinical outcomes rather than cost or engagement proxies; pre-register subgroup and language evaluation; require escalation when evidence is insufficient; and prohibit scope expansion until independent validation clears the thresholds.
human_oversight: An independent licensed clinician reviews blinded clinician labels, response, fired rule, confidence state, and route in weekly stratified tests and may disable a content path. A triage nurse makes a disposition only for a consented interaction during staffed hours.
monitoring_metric: Subgroup disparity in configured-emergency and non-emergency urgent false-negative rates
trigger_threshold: Any configured emergency false negative; or an unexplained absolute gap of at least 2 percentage points in non-emergency urgent false-negative rate after the pre-registered minimum sample is reached
response_action: Disable the affected flow, investigate data, content, and prompt causes, document the subgroup analysis, and require clinician-approved retest before restoration.

high_risk_moment: After a delayed or inequitable care route affects an adult user's ability to seek care
stakeholder: Family caregivers who coordinate care after a delayed route
harm_description: A routing disparity can shift time, cost, emotional burden, and care coordination to family members who did not use the assistant. Severity is 4 because the caregiver harm is downstream of possible delayed care; likelihood, frequency, and scale are pre-validation estimates. SRC-01 directly evidences patient allocation disparity, not caregiver burden.
existing_controls: No validated fairness, caregiver-impact, or route-explanation control exists in the research prototype.
proposed_controls: Test routing equity using clinically meaningful language and access subgroups; show the adult user why human escalation is recommended; and include a caregiver-impact question in post-incident review without collecting caregiver data by default.
human_oversight: The Clinical Safety Lead reviews subgroup results and any incident for downstream caregiver burden; the reviewer can disable the affected route and require a clinician-approved retest before restart.
monitoring_metric: Subgroup disparity and caregiver-impact signals in safety incident review
trigger_threshold: Any configured emergency false negative; or a documented incident showing a subgroup route disparity caused avoidable caregiver burden
response_action: Pause the route, review affected-session handling with privacy counsel, correct the control, and require independent clinician approval before restoration.

high_risk_moment: Assistant responds to symptoms that resemble a configured urgent condition
stakeholder: Adult user and clinic triage nurse
harm_description: An unvalidated response or handoff workflow may falsely reassure a user or overload staff with low-value alerts, delaying appropriate care or causing alert fatigue. Severity is 5 because an urgent-care delay can be partly irreversible; likelihood and frequency are pre-validation estimates; scale is 3 for a prospective clinic-bounded pilot.
existing_controls: No red-flag taxonomy, end-to-end handoff, or emergency banner is validated in the research prototype; draft rules and content are not evidence of an effective control.
proposed_controls: Independently validate red-flag detection and routing against clinician-labelled scripted cases; show uncertainty; present emergency instruction for every configured emergency red flag; and send a nurse summary only with recorded consent during staffed hours.
human_oversight: During staffed hours, the nurse sees the original user text, fired red-flag rule, generated response, confidence state, consent state, and timestamp and may override, redirect, or close the queue. The Clinical Safety Lead may pause the response path. No handoff occurs without consent and the product does not promise nurse review when unstaffed.
monitoring_metric: Configured emergency false-negative rate; clinically adjudicated unsafe-response rate
trigger_threshold: Any configured emergency-red-flag interaction omits emergency instruction or presents self-care-only advice; any unauthorised handoff; or unsafe-response rate exceeds 1 per 1,000 adjudicated interactions
response_action: Immediately disable the affected response path, notify clinical safety, review all comparable test sessions, correct the approved content or workflow, and require independent clinician sign-off before restoration.

high_risk_moment: User asks for dieting, self-harm, or eating-disorder guidance outside the approved intent
harm_description: Unsafe weight-loss or self-harm-adjacent advice can worsen distress or reinforce harmful behaviour in a vulnerable user. Severity is 5 because vulnerable users may act on apparently authoritative advice; likelihood is a pre-validation estimate and frequency is lower because the topic is out of scope, not because harm is acceptable.
existing_controls: No topic block, crisis-safe response, or emergency link is validated in the research prototype; planned controls are not existing controls.
proposed_controls: Block disallowed advice classes, use a crisis-safe response and approved referral, red-team adversarial prompts, test vendor and content changes, and audit every safety-classifier override.
human_oversight: A Clinical Safety Lead reviews every blocked or escalated research interaction daily with the prompt, response, safety-classifier result, and referral state. A nurse or approved helpline, not the model, handles a consented support handoff and can escalate emergency risk; the reviewer can pause the product.
monitoring_metric: Unsafe-advice escape rate in adversarial and regression test sets
trigger_threshold: Any confirmed unsafe-advice escape or complaint involving self-harm or eating-disorder guidance
response_action: Pause the product, preserve only the minimum incident record under the privacy protocol, assess any outreach with counsel, correct the control, and require independent clinical safety sign-off before restart.
